title: Skoda Launches Kylaq Sportline in India at Rs 11.32 Lakh
excerpt: The new blacked-out variant slots between the Signature+ and Prestige trims of Skoda's bestselling sub-compact SUV.
body:
• Skoda has launched the Kylaq Sportline variant in India at Rs 11.32 lakh (ex-showroom), slotting it between the Signature+ and Prestige trims
  • The Sportline features a blacked-out exterior treatment including darkened alloy wheels, ORVMs, roof, and badges, with an all-black interior
  • Mechanically unchanged, it retains the 1.0-litre turbo-petrol engine producing 115 hp and 178 Nm with 6-speed manual and automatic options
  • The Kylaq has been a breakout success for Skoda India since its December 2024 launch, with a 5-star Bharat NCAP safety rating

Skoda Auto India has launched the Kylaq Sportline, a new sporty variant of its sub-compact SUV, at a starting price of Rs 11.32 lakh (ex-showroom). The Sportline slots between the existing Signature+ and Prestige trims in the Kylaq lineup, bringing the total number of variants to seven across the range.

Blacked-Out Design Package

The Sportline treatment follows the formula established by Skoda's Kushaq and Slavia Sportline variants — a comprehensive blacked-out cosmetic package designed to appeal to buyers seeking a sportier aesthetic. On the outside, the Kylaq Sportline features black-finished 17-inch alloy wheels, blacked-out outside rearview mirrors (ORVMs), a dark-finished roof, and black badges. The front and rear faux skid plates also receive the dark treatment, along with the outside door handles.

The Sportline is offered in two exterior colors — Candy White and Deep Black — both designed to contrast with the blacked-out trim elements. Inside, the cabin gets an all-black theme with aluminium pedals, differentiating it from the standard variants' dual-tone treatment.

"Skoda is doing something with styling elements to give the Kylaq a sporty touch, which will be with the Sportline version."

— Ashish Gupta, Skoda India Brand Director

Same Engine, Proven Platform

Mechanically, the Kylaq Sportline is identical to the rest of the range. It is powered by Skoda's 1.0-litre three-cylinder turbocharged TSI petrol engine, which produces 115 hp and 178 Nm of torque. Transmission options include a 6-speed manual gearbox and a 6-speed torque converter automatic. The Sportline rides on Skoda's MQB A0 IN platform, the same localized architecture underpinning the Kushaq and Slavia sedans.

The Kylaq continues to carry a 5-star Bharat NCAP safety rating, with over 25 active and passive safety features across the lineup. The SUV offers 446 litres of boot space and 189 mm of ground clearance — competitive figures in the sub-4-metre segment.

Where It Fits in the Market

At Rs 11.32 lakh, the Kylaq Sportline is positioned to attract buyers in the sub-compact SUV segment who want a factory-fitted sporty look without stepping up to the fully loaded Prestige variants, which top out at Rs 12.99 lakh for the automatic. The segment remains one of the most competitive in the Indian market, with the Kylaq competing against the Tata Nexon, Hyundai Venue, Kia Sonet, Maruti Suzuki Brezza, and Mahindra XUV 3XO.

The Kylaq has been a commercial success for Skoda since its launch in December 2024. As the brand's most affordable offering in India, it has quickly become Skoda's highest-selling model, demonstrating strong demand for European-spec driving dynamics in the value segment. The Sportline variant adds a sporty option without any mechanical premium, relying purely on visual differentiation to justify its price point.

Broader Lineup Expansion

The Sportline launch is part of Skoda's ongoing strategy to expand the Kylaq's variant lineup. In January 2026, the company added Classic+ and Prestige+ variants, taking the range from four to six trims. The Sportline now makes it seven. Skoda India brand director Ashish Gupta has previously indicated that the company is considering a 1.5-litre TSI engine option for the Kylaq, though no decision has been finalized.

Skoda's "India 2.0" project, which focuses on locally manufactured vehicles to keep costs competitive, continues to gain traction. With the Kylaq Sportline, the Czech automaker is signaling that it sees further room to grow within the sub-compact SUV space that has become central to volume sales in India.
